q: The 32-bit value 0x0A0B0C0D is written to memory on a little-endian machine. What is the byte sequence, lowest address first?
exp: Little-endian stores the least significant byte at the lowest address. The least significant byte of 0x0A0B0C0D is 0x0D, so the order is 0D 0C 0B 0A — a straight reversal of the bytes. Option (a) is the big-endian layout. Option (c) swaps within pairs only, a common distractor.

q: Which scheduling algorithm gives provably minimum average waiting time?
exp: SJF is optimal for average waiting time — this can be proved by an exchange argument: swapping any adjacent pair so the shorter job runs first never increases total waiting time. Its practical problem is that burst length must be known in advance, so real systems estimate it by exponential averaging of past bursts. Note the question asks about average waiting time, not response time; Round Robin is the one favouring response time.

q: In the Two-Phase Commit protocol, the principal weakness is that

opts.B: participants may block indefinitely if the coordinator fails after voting
opts.C: it does not guarantee atomicity across sites

exp: 2PC is a blocking protocol.
